findings.text: Provides the per-VCPU trap refresh operation; it updates hypervisor control state for the calling VCPU and ensures VM-wide fine-grained trap data is built once.
Computes the stored mask for a single fine-grained trap group from associated descriptor tables.
Returns the pair of fixed reservation masks for a requested virtualized control register, or empty masks for unlisted inputs.
Finalizes guest-visible identification state before first run, including nested-register preparation and GIC-related fixups that depend on irqchip presence.
Initializes the VM-wide sanitised-register mask table for nested guests exactly once, then refreshes every sanitised register view on the calling VCPU.
Idempotent mapping entry for virtual distributor resources; repeated calls after readiness succeed without further work.
Establishes device-type second-stage mappings for a guest address interval backed by supplied host addresses.
Fine-grained trap values are formed by unioning unsupported-feature contributions treated as reserved, without considering intrinsic register reservations or existence.

Reservation accumulation skips entries that fail required flags or hit excluded flags, determines support through forced failure, callback, or ID comparison, applies an E2H-mode gate, and files unsupported bits into either the zero or one accumulator based on descriptor attributes and current mode.
Support test extracts a field from the VM ID register image and compares against a descriptor limit using signed semantics when requested and unsigned semantics otherwise.
Bit selection yields either the union of a referenced mask pair or a directly stored bit pattern, chosen by a descriptor flag.

Per-VCPU hypervisor control setup handles virtualization-host extensions, routes external aborts and error-record traps when reliability extensions exist, enables write-back handling when stage-two support exists, selects a cache-visibility trap level from event and cache-type capabilities plus counter equality, adjusts width handling for 32-bit guests, chooses between memory-tagging enable and an alternate trap, and traps range TLB maintenance when the relevant ISA feature is absent.

Interrupt-controller hypervisor control gains trap-all behavior only when the host offers the newer controller and the guest either selects the older model or lacks a kernel irqchip; otherwise it is left unchanged.
Host controller capability is reported true when global state indicates either native version three or compatibility through version five.

Register-level reservation combines per-bit feature results with whole-register fixed masks, then forces every non-reserved bit of an unsupported register into the zero set while clearing any overlap from the one set.
Mask installation accepts only indices inside the sanitised window and delegates storage to the VM setter.
Identification-register writes are rejected after the VM has run or for unknown selectors, and otherwise update the stored image.
Final GIC visibility clears the three GIC-related fields and then sets values appropriate to the chosen virtual controller model and 32-bit support.
Nested VGIC per-VCPU setup ensures a maintenance interrupt identifier exists by installing a default when unset, then records the calling VCPU as owner.
Distributor device setup chooses a region table according to controller generation and advertises a smaller window for the older generation than for the newer one.

Older-generation mapping requires both base addresses to be defined and disjoint, ensures dynamic structures exist, registers the CPU-interface device, and conditionally adds a direct physical mapping unless a trap mode is active.
The VM configuration mutex serializes trap calculation, finalization, nested mask creation, ID writes, and VGIC resource mapping; several paths assert it is held.
Resource mapping nests the slot mutex outside the configuration mutex with early release before distributor registration, while address mapping holds the MMU write lock around each page insertion.
Distributor readiness uses an acquire check for fast return, a locked recheck, registration work, then a release store; mapping failure marks the VM dead.
A VM flag records completion of fine-grained trap construction so later VCPU trap refreshes skip reconstruction.
Reservation state is represented as two independent accumulators, one for must-be-zero and one for must-be-one contributions.
Unrecognized trap-group and distributor-type inputs follow fatal paths, while unlisted fixed-bit registers and unknown VGIC models warn and continue with safe defaults.
Address mapping refuses protected guests, aligns the guest base down and extends length for the offset, iterates page by page with cache top-up, and always releases the cache.
Distributor window length is four kilobytes for generation two and sixty-four kilobytes for generation three.
